accuracy.evidence: Every number was checked by stoichiometry with Ar values from the AQA data sheet: CaCO₃ (Mr 100) → CO₂ (Mr 44), so 2.00 g of marble gives 0.88 g CO₂ (152.40 → 151.52 g); 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO with Mg 24 and MgO 40, so 0.24 g Mg gives 0.40 g MgO and 0.16 g O₂ (25.24 → 25.40 g on a 25.00 g crucible); CuCO₃ (Mr 123.5) → CuO (79.5) + CO₂ (44), so 12.35 g gives 7.95 g and 4.40 g. The specification wording was checked against AQA GCSE Chemistry 4.3.1.2 and the standards against NGSS MS-PS1-5. The balloon upthrust caveat is stated as a small effect, not a failure of conservation.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented errors from the AQA examiner reports and the RSC misconceptions guide: 'mass is destroyed or used up' (prediction 1 option 'Stay the same: mass is conserved', challenge 'destroy', m6), 'burning always makes things lighter' (prediction 2 'goes down: burning uses it up', challenge 'burn', m2, contrast with wood in m9), adding instead of subtracting readings (sum feedback 'Do not add the readings', challenge 'add'), taking the whole oxide mass as the oxygen (challenge 'whole', sum 2), expecting a sealed flask to change (challenge 'sealed', 'gain') and thinking any open reaction changes mass even with no gas (sort cards for precipitation and neutralisation, challenge 'solid', 'slow').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagmsys is built on a balance reading that responds to whether the system is open: the same reaction gives 152.40 → 151.52 g open and a flat 152.40 g with the stopper in, a crucible reading climbs only when the lid is lifted until two readings match (heating to constant mass), and a step-planning board rejects an open flask or weighing only the solid. flagburn is about combustion products and oxygen supply, flagstsym about state symbols and the 'sealed' visual only toggles a lid on one equation; none heats to constant mass or computes gas mass from readings. The lab_distinct gate passed under 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: Students discover the rule by running it: they see the open reading fall and the sealed one not move, then watch magnesium gain mass heat by heat. The sort step asks the single question that decides every case (is a gas made or used, and can it get out or in?), the sums make the 'difference = gas' rule concrete with four data sets, and the plan step turns the idea into an experiment. Each completion line restates the rule.

predictions.evidence: Both predictions carry the most tempting wrong idea and the lab then disproves it: 'Stay the same: mass is conserved' for the open flask (disproved when the balance falls by 0.88 g, then explained by the sealed run) and 'goes down: burning uses it up' for magnesium (disproved as the reading climbs to 25.40 g).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Twelve wrong-answer messages, each naming the slip: destroyed mass (destroy), density confusion (dense), burning means lighter (burn), open iron staying the same (same), sealed flask falling (sealed) or rising (gain), adding readings (add), taking the whole oxide (whole), open beaker as closed (open), lid off as closed (lid), solids having no mass (solid) and speed mattering (slow). Six questions rotate, so a retry gives a new item.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs stay short and concrete (one case per paragraph: open with gas out, gas in from the air, closed system, using the difference); the validator's family readability limits passed for kid and adult text. Lab prompts are brief. The adult text uses the precise terms closed and non-enclosed system, conservation of mass, constant mass, upthrust and balanced symbol equations.

no_filler.evidence: No warm-up or summary padding; the content gate found no banned phrases and explanation overlap stayed under 12% against every lesson, including lesson 47 Conservation of mass. Feedback lines each give a fact or an operation, for example 'Subtract, do not add: 0.80 − 0.48 = 0.32 g of oxygen.'

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots in light theme for all 6 steps: the flask and balance display read clearly at 390 px with the run summary on one line, the crucible step shows the reading and the readings list, the three sort bins share the width with wrapped labels, the four answer keys sit in a 2 by 2 grid and the six plan cards wrap to two lines inside their tiles. Every action has a full-size button under the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: The walkthrough gate completed all five tasks with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) reported no violations in light or dark. Every canvas tap or drag has a labelled button ('Start the reaction and watch the balance', 'Heat and lift the lid', 'Answer 0.88 g'), and the canvas aria-label is rewritten with each reading and feedback message.
